## 2

I understand why some images can seem easy to fake, especially when we mostly experience space through photographs and videos. But the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on one set of pictures: ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible from different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses is round, and people and planes can travel around the globe. Satellites, GPS, weather forecasting, and communications also rely on measurements consistent with a round Earth. These observations come from many independent sources, not one organization producing identical images.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors, like the colors in a rainbow. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in many directions more strongly than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky.

Violet is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to it, and some violet light is absorbed higher in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere, scattering away much of the blue and leaving more red, orange, and pink light for us to see.

雨下了一整夜，城市像被一层透明的薄纱笼住。路灯昏黄，雨丝在光里交织成细密的网，积水倒映着摇晃的树影和偶尔驶过的车灯。屋檐不停滴水，发出轻轻的声响，仿佛有人在黑暗中耐心敲门。远处的高楼沉默地伫立着，窗子里零星亮着温暖的灯。风吹过湿漉漉的街道，带来泥土、青草和雨水的清凉气息。夜很深，世界却没有完全沉睡。
